coaching.headline: First Fangtooth was ours. Every one after that came within a minute of one of our deaths.
coaching.team: We drew first blood and took the first Fangtooth, then watched them take all four Fangtooth and Primal Fangtooth spawns after it and finish with ten structures to our four. Each of those Fangtooth takes came within a minute of at least one of our deaths. Countess and Belica brought the damage; Rampage and Argus kept collecting bodies.
coaching.lossReflection: When one of us is dead and their Fangtooth is close, give it up and hit something on the other side. After the first Fangtooth they took, we won a fight and took Mini Prime, the only won fight we turned into a prize. A conceded stack is cheaper than a stack plus more bodies, though it promises nothing.

focus.title: Count heads before Fangtooth
focus.action: Before every Fangtooth, count who is alive. If anyone is dead or we just lost an exchange, call a tower or Mini Prime on the far side instead of shoving a short-handed team into another fight.

23.5.call: Four of us were credited in this 1-3 exchange shortly before their Fangtooth, and a second 1-2 sequence followed in the same window. After losing the first exchange, back off together and take a wave; the record cannot show whether the pit was ever contestable.

37.4.call: Argus took all three kills in this 0-3 sequence, and the enemy took the Primal Fangtooth in the same window. The record does not show who engaged or how the team arrived, so the check is simple: be grouped before the Primal timer.

39.8.call: We took Orb Prime while losing four heroes in a 0-4 sequence, and the Core fell shortly after with all three inhibitors already gone. With the base open, only commit to Orb Prime if we can still get back to defend; the record cannot show who hit the Core.

matchup: Countess killed lane opponent Scarlett three times and died to her twice.
Rampage was the bigger match-wide threat: physical damage, growing Behemoth healing, and a share of their team kill lead.
build: A full ability-damage build; Megacosm and Tainted Scepter suit Rampage's health and regeneration.
eternal: This setup fits a Countess dealing most damage through spells.
The Tenth Seal is a draft alternative to Lich for Feast uptime, giving up the sustain that suits a melee mage.
augment: Sanguine Slash pays when Countess catches a lone target and adds nothing in a crowded brawl.
Shadow Strike is the draft alternative if Shadow Slip repositioning matters more, trading away the isolated-target bonus.
crest: Tempest damages nearby heroes and heals, suiting a Countess staying inside a fight alongside Blade Siphon.
improvement: Keep the damage package: Countess led our hero damage with three deaths.
Spellbreaker's magical armor does nothing against Scarlett's physical damage or Rampage's basic attacks.
If they end fights before Feast lands, compare a physical armor item, trading burst for surviving the first engage.

matchup: Argus punishes a mage standing still and got three kills on Belica.
Neural Disruptor and Void Drone both work against Argus's mana-hungry kit.
build: Spellbreaker blocks one ability, a direct answer to Argus's stun orb.
Caustica ignores part of magical armor from Steel or Scarlett's Absolution.
eternal: A mana and economy setup that fits a spell-heavy mid.
Perfection is a draft alternative to Runic Focus for ability haste while healthy, giving up mana-scaled power.
augment: Combat Veteran is a scaling pick with no fight effect of its own.
Devastating Bombs is the draft alternative if Void Bomb lands on isolated targets, trading experience for burst.
The match does not show either would have changed the deaths.
crest: Soulbearer is the build's only active defensive item, so hold it for a Scarlett, Argus or Rampage engage.
improvement: Keep the damage package; its damage rate was far above this player's Belica baseline.
If Scarlett or Rampage keep closing the gap, compare Combustion with a physical armor slot, trading splash for surviving the engage.
That is conditional; the record does not show which deaths it would have changed.

matchup: Feng Mao got the first two kills on Rampage, then Rampage killed Feng Mao three straight times and four in all.
Behemoth, tenacity healing and doubled jungle regeneration make Rampage hard to duel.
build: The damage suits Rampage's health and armor, but nothing here adds armor against a physical-heavy enemy team.
eternal: Knell suits a duelist sticking to one target.
Its armor only arrives while hitting heroes, so it is not protection on the way into a fight.
augment: Ichorous Glaive helps clears and rewards finishing low targets with Earth Shatter.
Imperial Duelist is a draft alternative for a straight fight with Rampage, trading away the kill sustain.
crest: Ortus rewards a jungler already getting takedowns, which this match rarely gave Feng Mao.
improvement: If Rampage keeps killing Feng Mao, compare a physical armor item over Sky Splitter, trading current-health damage for survival.
Once Rampage is ahead, meet Rampage only with a teammate close enough to follow; no item makes a solo fight safe.

matchup: Wraith killed Sparrow three times outside detected fights; Camouflage and a long sniper shot make Wraith a pick threat.
Steel's projectile wall can cut Sparrow's shots off, and Argus finished three later deaths.
build: A coherent basic-attack build; Demolisher and Tainted Rounds suit Steel, Rampage and Scarlett.
Nothing in it protects against a pick.
eternal: Heightened Senses and the Pacifier dash both trigger Wind-Rider.
Natural Resistance is the draft alternative to Forage if getting caught keeps happening, trading farm income for a low-health cleanse.
augment: Keep Endless Hunt as a scaling choice, but this match gave it few takedowns.
It does nothing to prevent the deaths that starved it.
crest: Pacifier's dash is the build's only repositioning tool, so hold it for a Wraith or Rampage engage.
improvement: If Wraith and Rampage keep finding Sparrow, compare a defensive slot against Imperator.
Protection buys time for Zinx's heal and revival; Imperator adds critical damage.
Treat it as a conditional swap, not the cause of the loss.

matchup: Five of Zinx's seven deaths came from Rampage and Wraith.
Rampage's leap, boulder stun and Behemoth sustain make Rampage the main threat to plan around.
build: An attack-focused support build that suits Sparrow's basic attacks rather than a healing one.
The two Greaves were our team's only physical armor against Rampage, Scarlett and Wraith.
eternal: Neural Regenesis is a revival, so Peal only pays if Zinx keeps attacking afterward.
augment: Disc Of Demise means more Ricochet stuns, though Rampage gains tenacity and healing when immobilized.
Heal Matrix is the draft alternative: two Infuse charges at slightly lower healing.
crest: Tranquility heals Zinx and nearby allies with brief mitigation.
Zinx placed six wards to Steel's fifteen; totals cannot show how often the higher cap was filled.
improvement: Keep the armor boots against this physical-heavy team.
If Rampage keeps reaching Zinx, compare Orion with a protective support item, trading personal damage for keeping Sparrow alive.
That is conditional; the record does not show which deaths it would have changed.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324 on Countess led our hero damage, killed Scarlett three times while dying to Scarlett twice, and died only three times all game. That is a fucking solid offlane line. Keep it.
When Rampage goes Behemoth, the healing climbs with every one of us nearby. If Countess can reach Rampage without diving past Argus, land the Tainted Scepter damage there first; Scarlett can wait.
10edbf65-457d-48d0-9151-9df5b4fcb40a: Willy Guggenheim brought the violence: nine kills and a damage rate way above the baseline on Belica. Keep that output exactly as it is.

Belica's death outside any detected fight came just before their first Primal Fangtooth. With a Primal timer close, send Void Drone ahead to check the approach and stay behind the team until it shows clear.
a412baf3-dd17-4f89-8ecf-9d0704f3a79e: Xeebs got the first two kills on Rampage, then Rampage killed Feng Mao three straight times. Ten deaths is a fucking buffet for the enemy jungler, and Rampage ate four plates personally.
Once Rampage is ahead, do not take a duel with Rampage. Ping where Rampage last showed, farm and pressure the opposite side, and only meet Rampage with Countess or Belica close enough to follow.
dfc1532a-f881-4efe-a48b-df67882e88f7: Sparrow took first blood off Wraith, farmed well and led our objective damage. Then Wraith killed Sparrow three times outside any detected fight, and one of those came right before two outer towers fell.
When Wraith goes camouflaged or drops out of vision, play at max range behind Countess or Zinx and save the Pacifier dash for the follow-up. Seven deaths is way too long spent getting tea-bagged.
13ff3597-dd39-48be-891f-1a230e8e312e: xIGAGAIx had a rough Zinx game: seven deaths and a hand in only a fifth of our kills. Rampage killed Zinx three times, and one of those came just before their Fangtooth.
When Rampage is missing from the map, stay glued to Sparrow or Belica with Ricochet ready for the engage. A support Rampage reaches with nobody close is a free meal.

threats: Heal-stacking: Steel. Anti-heal is mandatory against this comp — we brought 2 items of it.
synergy: Our engage/CC: Countess Feast (suppress 0.75s), Lt. Belica Neural Disruptor (silence 0.5s). Our kills come from landing burst INSIDE that CC window — whoever lands it, the rest must follow up immediately.
We have sustain (Zinx) — favor the longer fight where our heals out-grind them.
Strong AoE/teamfight kit — group at choke points and fight on top of objectives.

rampage.loadout: Krix (Regenerative Tissue + Predator), augment Tiny Titan, crest Saphir's Mantle
lines: Lead story: Damage well above normal. 1,148 hero damage a minute, more than 94% of Rampage jungle players this patch (30% of the team's). The damage came from Overlord, Rapture, Gaia Greaves.
Behemoth at top rank: 110s base, about 100s by the end (9% shorter) from 10 ability haste: Gaia Greaves 10.
Their build heals off damage: anti-heal (the Tainted items) cuts it.
Rampage dealt 47,069 hero damage, 30% of their team's, with +50 physical power from items.
Overlord (item): On Successful Basic Attack: Deal (+1%) Damage. Deal (+30%) (+2.5%) Damage around the Target. Damage decreases from 100% to 50% based on distance.
Rapture (item): While within 475u of an Enemy Unit: Your Basic Attacks deal 20 (+2.5%)(+15%) Damage On-Hit to them.
Gaia Greaves (item): Move to generate up to 100 stacks: Stacks grant up to 40 Movement Speed. Basic Attacks expend all stacks for bonus Damage. Deals up to 40 (+60%)(+5%) Damage.
Cursed Scroll (item): On Basic Attack: Deal 20 (+3.5%) Damage to yourself and the Enemy Target. This damage cannot hurt you below 35% Health.

Saphir's Mantle (crest): Increase your Size and Max Health by 10% for 6s. Deal 60 (+1.25%) Damage to nearby Heroes. After the duration, permanently increase your Max Health by 20% of the Damage dealt.
Predator (Eternal minor): Camp Leader kills grant 10% Bonus Damage and 4% Movement Speed for 20s, with 100% bonus duration for Epic Monsters.
Tiny Titan (augment): Behemoth shrinks Rampage instead, granting him 25/27.5/30% Total Attack Speed, but he receives 45% more damage.
Sustain: 7% omnivamp; 49,897 healing recorded.
Toughness: +1455 health, +98 physical armor, +35 magical armor; took 109,776 damage, mitigated 78,328, died 5 times.
